extracted.subtask_description: Compare typefaces and point sizes by examining repeated sample text set in multiple typefaces and point sizes; use specimens to decide body/display sizes, spacing, and glyph design for book or print typography.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specimens of types in use
rubrics_metrics.description: The page presents the same passage (Polybius on the fall of Carthage and Corinth) repeatedly set in a variety of point sizes and labelled specimens (e.g., FIVE POINT NO. 83, SIX POINT NO. 57, SEVEN POINT NO. 57, EIGHT POINT NO. 57, etc.), and in different named styles (e.g., OLD STYLE BODY TYPE, MONOTYPE TYPE).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these side-by-side specimens to observe how a single text reads and appears across different point sizes and type styles; headings identify size and specimen number to facilitate comparison. Examples on the page span many sizes (5–18 point and named specimen sets).

rubrics_metrics.name: Choose appropriate point size for body or display text
rubrics_metrics.description: Multiple versions of the same passage are shown in different point sizes (five point, six point, seven point, eight point, nine point, ten point, eleven, twelve, fourteen, eighteen point, etc.), demonstrating how readability and emphasis change with size.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select smaller point sizes only where legibility is acceptable (e.g., captions, compact settings) and larger sizes for display/headings; consult the specimen lines to judge at intended reading distance. The specimens illustrate relative weight, x-height, and readability at each size.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use consistent sample text for comparison
rubrics_metrics.description: The same excerpt is repeatedly used across specimens so that differences between faces and sizes can be directly compared.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep sample text consistent when evaluating type so that letterforms, spacing, and overall color of the page can be compared without content variation influencing judgement. The page's repeated passage is explicitly intended for this purpose.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluate headings and emphasis treatments (all-caps and display lines)
rubrics_metrics.description: Specimens include lines in full capitals and contrasted display lines (e.g., 'A WORLD-EMPIRE...' in all caps, headings like 'OLD STYLE BODY TYPE'), showing how caps and display settings read at various sizes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the capitalized/display lines to judge how all-caps or emphasized settings affect readability, word color, and overall page rhythm at each point size; note that all-caps can become heavy or lose distinctiveness at very small sizes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compare typeface families/styles (old style, monotype, etc.)
rubrics_metrics.description: The book labels different specimen groups (for example, 'OLD STYLE BODY TYPE', 'MONOTYPE TYPE') and shows the same passage in those different families to demonstrate tonal and structural differences between type styles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose a type family based on the tone, readability, and suitability for the work (e.g., old style for traditional book text, monotype for mechanical or monospaced needs); compare specimens to assess contrast, serif shape, stroke modulation, and suitability for body vs. display.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assess line length, leading, and page color
rubrics_metrics.description: Specimens show variations in line breaks, line lengths, and spacing (leading) as the same passage is set at different sizes and in different specimen blocks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Observe how leading and line length interact with point size to affect the 'color' of the text block and readability; use specimens to determine comfortable line length and appropriate leading for the intended point size and medium.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examine glyphs, numeral design, and special-character spacing
rubrics_metrics.description: Specimens include sequences of vowels, special glyph clusters, and repeated numerals (e.g., 'AEIOU', '1234567890', strings of 'aeiou', and other character samples) to reveal forms, kerning, and spacing behaviour.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these glyph- and numeral-specific samples to check numeral style, punctuation appearance, diacritics, kerning issues, and the distinctiveness of individual letterforms across sizes; such lines help spot problems not visible in running text.
